leadStory.title: Security tightens outside Union Minister Pralhad Joshi's Hubballi residence as sugarcane farmers intensify protest
leadStory.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
leadStory.summary: Hubballi (Karnataka) [India], October 13 A day after Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar met Union Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister Pralhad Joshi in the national capital, sec
content: Hubballi (Karnataka) [India], October 13 A day after Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar met Union Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister Pralhad Joshi in the national capital, security at the latter's residence in Hubballi district was tightened on Tuesday amid calls for a national highway blockade by the sugarcane farmers.

The farmers have intensified their demands while pressing for a hike in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for sugarcane. They have announced a road blockade on the National Highway. Farmers have also been demanding that their long-standing demands be implemented.
As this happened, a heavy police force was deployed, and barricades were erected on roads leading to the minister's residence.

The development comes amid an ongoing dispute over sugarcane pricing and alleged irregularities at sugar factories, with farmers raising concerns over weighing discrepancies, lower recorded harvest weights, alleged tampering with weighing machines and transportation-related fraud after harvesting.
Joshi met Karnataka CM Shivakumar at the former's residence in Delhi on Monday to discuss concerns raised by sugarcane farmers over pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season.
In a post on X, Joshi wrote, "Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who arrived at my residence in Delhi this evening, met me cordially.

"In this context, at meeting with sugarcane farmers, the major issues shared by the farmers were the govt advisory price for sugarcane, fraud and discrepancies in sugarcane weighing at sugar factories, factories showing lower harvest weights, tampering with weighing machines, and paying attention to transportation fraud after harvest. I informed the Chief Minister about these problems and requested resolution."

Meanwhile, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar wrote on X, "Met Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Joshi Pralhad, to discuss the concerns of Karnataka's sugarcane farmers regarding cane pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season."

"We discussed the need to ensure fair and remunerative prices for sugarcane growers and to address the concerns raised by our farmers. I urged the Union Government to consider Karnataka's views and safeguard the interests of sugarcane farmers."

Earlier on Monday, while speaking to Metrotimes, Shivakumar said, "I came here to discuss the sugarcane price issue. Farmers are demanding a higher price, but factories are unable to meet their demands due to heavy losses. This year, there has also been a severe drought. More than 200 farmers had come to meet me. I had also sent some of our ministers to discuss the issue."

"This matter needs to be discussed at the national level. It is not just Karnataka's problem. Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and every state where sugarcane is grown need to take a decision. There will be a process of consultation. We have said that we all need to work together to help everyone. The farmers should benefit, and the industries should also benefit. We will work on this issue," he added.

trendingNews.title: WhatsApp to block logins on outdated iOS and Android versions: What users need to know
trendingNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
trendingNews.summary: Washington [US], October 6 WhatsApp is rolling out a new server-side security measure that will block users from logging into their accounts if their devices are running outdated versions of iOS or An
content: Washington [US], October 6 WhatsApp is rolling out a new server-side security measure that will block users from logging into their accounts if their devices are running outdated versions of iOS or Android, as per reports by GSM Arena.

Unlike conventional app updates delivered through app stores, the new restriction is being deployed through WhatsApp's servers. This means users may encounter the block even without installing a specific new version of the messaging app.
If a device's operating system is considered too old, WhatsApp will prevent the app from opening to its usual chat interface and instead show a dedicated blocking screen.

The screen will instruct users to update their phone's operating system through system settings before access can be restored. It will also provide information on how to check the operating system version currently installed on the device.

trendingNews.title: India's power sector profits likely to grow up to 11% in Q2FY27 on strong demand: Report
trendingNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
trendingNews.summary: New Delhi [India], October 13 India's power sector is expected to post up to 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) profit growth in Q2FY27, driven by strong electricity demand, higher plant load factors and
content: New Delhi [India], October 13 India's power sector is expected to post up to 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) profit growth in Q2FY27, driven by strong electricity demand, higher plant load factors and potential incentives for thermal power producers, according to Nuvama Institutional Equities.

Nuvama noted in its report, India's power demand rose nearly 12 per cent YoY to 163 billion units (BU) in September 2026 and 11.7 per cent to 503 BU in Q2FY27. This was largely due to high humidity and lower average rainfall.
On the other hand, "peak power demand surged ~17.5% YoY to 269GW in Sep-26, led by non-solar hour demand."
Meanwhile, India's thermal power accounted for nearly 69 per cent of total generation in Q2FY27, with plant load factors (PLFs) rising to 68.3 per cent from 61.9 per cent in Q2FY26.

Apart from this, tighter power supply pushed electricity prices higher on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), with solar-hour prices remaining elevated. Additionally, non-solar-hour prices also increased in September on YoY basis.

indiaNews.title: "Punjab gov is being run by drug mafia": Manjinder Singh Sirsa blames AAP govt for anti-drug activist’s murder
indiaNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
indiaNews.summary: New Delhi [India], October 13 Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab, alleging a direct nexus between the administ
content: New Delhi [India], October 13 Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab, alleging a direct nexus between the administration and the "drug mafia" following the murder of Anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota in Mansa.
Addressing the reporters, Sirsa claimed that the incident highlights a state of lawlessness similar to cartel-run nations.

"A very major incident occurred just a short while ago. As we have been saying repeatedly, the Punjab government is being run by a drug mafia. It seems that Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal, and Manish Sisodia are taking a lot of money from the drug mafia," Sirsa alleged.
Drawing a grim comparison, Sirsa argued that Punjab is witnessing an unprecedented decline in public safety for those challenging the illicit narcotics trade.
"Today, a Mansa-based drug activist—whom the Punjab police had previously arrested and tortured just because he spoke out against drugs—has now been murdered," he stated.

"Just imagine, this kind of thing used to happen in America or Colombia, where those who spoke out against drugs were killed. Today, Punjab has become the same kind of state, where the police either torture people and put them in jail, or, as in today's incident, someone who was fighting against drugs was murdered. This shows the state of drug issues in Punjab," he added.

Sirsa's remarks come after Jhota, who was known for his activism against drugs in Mansa, was shot by a medical shop owner. He was taken to a hospital after sustaining bullet injuries and later succumbed to them.

The killing of Jhota has ignited a political firestorm with opposition leaders tearing into the Bhagwant Mann-led government alleging a failure of law and order and questioning the effectiveness of the state's campaign against drugs.

Former Punjab Congress president Raja Warring, in a post on X said, "The daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota is a direct result of the failed law & order and failed 'Yudh Nashean Virudh' of the @BhagwantMann govt. Parminder stood up against Punjab's drug menace but his initiatives were never supported by the @AAPPunjab govt. His broad daylight murder exposes Serious failures of the AAP Govt."
Congress leader Sukhpal Singh Khaira also targeted the AAP government, alleging that the killing exposed the failure of its anti-drug campaign.

"The broad daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota a known and drug activist of Punjab only shows how powerful #DrugMafia is under the @AamAadmiParty govt! Politician-Police-Drug Mafia nexus rules the roost in Punjab," Khaira said in a post on X.
Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia alleged that Jhota was shot while recording drug dealers on camera.
"Parvinder Jhotta, who was fighting against the drug menace in Mansa, was shot at and subsequently died," Majithia said.
Sukhbir Badal, President of the Shiromani Akali DaI also slammed the state government accusing them of criminal negligence.

"I am profoundly shocked to learn about the merciless killing of Parvinder Singh Jhota by a drug trafficker. This heinous murder is a stark reminder that law and order has ceased to exist in Punjab. The deceased had been continuously raising his voice against the drug menace but no one took heed and no one supported him. The much-hyped Yudh Nashian Virudh is nothing but a gimmick and has completely failed. Recent events have exposed how the Guru-Dokhi Bhagwant Mann led AAP dispensation is completely engrossed in looting Punjab and draining the state's resources to enrich itself. They have zero attention towards the fast deteriorating situation in the state, and it is because of this criminal negligence that Punjabis are suffering every single day. This jungle raj must end," he asserted.

sportsNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
sportsNews.summary: Dubai [UAE], October 13 Indian skipper Shubman Gill achieved his record-extending fifth 'ICC Player of the Month' award for September 2026, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Tuesday
content: Dubai [UAE], October 13 Indian skipper Shubman Gill achieved his record-extending fifth 'ICC Player of the Month' award for September 2026, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Tuesday.
Gill, as per the ICC, won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza.
Gill scored 333 runs in India's first two ODIs against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets.
In the first ODI, in Thiruvananthapuram on 27 September, Gill made 110 off 108 balls as India chased down West Indies' 295/7. India reached the target of 296 in 41.4 overs.

Three days later in Guwahati, West Indies made 405/7, their first ODI total above 400. Gill, captaining India, responded with an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, including 26 fours and eight sixes, and India finished on 406/2 in 43.3 overs with 39 balls to spare. He reached his hundred in 62 balls, the fastest by an Indian captain in ODIs, and his double century in 117 balls, the fastest in ODI history.

It remains the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase. Gill and Rohit Sharma (101 off 75 balls) put on 255 for the opening wicket, India's highest partnership on home soil. The chase was the second-highest successful one in ODI history, behind only South Africa's 438/9 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.

content: New Delhi [India], October 13 India's power sector is expected to post up to 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) profit growth in Q2FY27, driven by strong electricity demand, higher plant load factors and potential incentives for thermal power producers, according to Nuvama Institutional Equities.

Nuvama noted in its report, India's power demand rose nearly 12 per cent YoY to 163 billion units (BU) in September 2026 and 11.7 per cent to 503 BU in Q2FY27. This was largely due to high humidity and lower average rainfall.
On the other hand, "peak power demand surged ~17.5% YoY to 269GW in Sep-26, led by non-solar hour demand."
Meanwhile, India's thermal power accounted for nearly 69 per cent of total generation in Q2FY27, with plant load factors (PLFs) rising to 68.3 per cent from 61.9 per cent in Q2FY26.

Apart from this, tighter power supply pushed electricity prices higher on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), with solar-hour prices remaining elevated. Additionally, non-solar-hour prices also increased in September on YoY basis.

MeitY noted that the field deployment reflects BHASHINI's "Voice-First Multilingual AI approach," which aims to expand access to communication tools and digital public services through speech-driven systems.

businessNews.title: Bisleri International Promotes Responsible Waste Management as Official Hydration Partner of the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026
businessNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
businessNews.summary: New Delhi [India], October 13: Bisleri International, India's leading packaged drinking water brand, collaborated with the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026 as its Official Hydration Partner. Held at Dr A
content: New Delhi [India], October 13: Bisleri International, India's leading packaged drinking water brand, collaborated with the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026 as its Official Hydration Partner. Held at Dr Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, the festival brought together over 1,000 school students, and educators, climate experts, artists and innovators under the theme 'AI & Climate: Reimagining the Future Together.' The festival forms part of the Purple Umbrella Foundation's wider mission to empower one million young climate champions. Bisleri's flagship Bottles for Change initiative played a central role in sensitising young participants on responsible plastic waste management, recycling and circularity.

As part of the collaboration, Bisleri created a dedicated 'Greener Promise' experience designed to help students see plastic waste as a resource that can be recovered, recycled and reimagined. At the centre of the experience was Wings of Change, an art installation created from 2,000 used PET bottles, using creative expression to bring the idea of circularity to life. The company also showcased its Benches of Dreams, made from recycled plastic, offering participants a tangible example of how discarded material can return to everyday use in a new form.

Speaking about the association, Dr Angelo George, CEO, Bisleri International, said, "It is vital to engage young people in conversations about environmental responsibility and inspire them to turn awareness into action. The Purple Umbrella Festival offers students an opportunity to learn, exchange ideas and make more sustainable choices in their everyday lives. Through Bottles for Change, we continue to build awareness of responsible plastic waste management and recycling, encouraging everyone to play their part in creating a cleaner, greener planet."

Aligned with the Purple Umbrella Foundation's larger mission of empowering one million young climate champions, the festival encouraged young people to explore climate change as creators, problem-solvers and emerging climate champions. Theatre, film, technology, innovation and dialogue were central to these interactions. The programme featured Theatre for Climate, short films and documentaries, student innovations, climate talks, a Climate, Health & Mental Wellbeing Conclave, and the Climate & Heritage Quiz.

Neeraj Kumar, Founder, Purple Umbrella Foundation, said, "The Purple Umbrella Festival is designed to encourage young people to think creatively about climate challenges and the role they can play in addressing them. Bisleri's participation adds an important dimension to the festival by helping students understand the importance of responsible plastic waste management and recycling through hands-on experiences."

Bisleri's participation at the festival reinforced its commitment to advancing responsible plastic waste management and environmental awareness among young people. Through Bottles for Change, the company continues to promote recycling and circularity while encouraging more responsible waste-management choices at the individual and community level.

techNews.summary: Washington [US], October 6 WhatsApp is rolling out a new server-side security measure that will block users from logging into their accounts if their devices are running outdated versions of iOS or An
content: Washington [US], October 6 WhatsApp is rolling out a new server-side security measure that will block users from logging into their accounts if their devices are running outdated versions of iOS or Android, as per reports by GSM Arena.

Unlike conventional app updates delivered through app stores, the new restriction is being deployed through WhatsApp's servers. This means users may encounter the block even without installing a specific new version of the messaging app.
If a device's operating system is considered too old, WhatsApp will prevent the app from opening to its usual chat interface and instead show a dedicated blocking screen.

The screen will instruct users to update their phone's operating system through system settings before access can be restored. It will also provide information on how to check the operating system version currently installed on the device.

techNews.title: Review of  Sony BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7, Sub 8, Rear 8
techNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
techNews.summary: New Delhi [India], October 3 I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series a
content: New Delhi [India], October 3 I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series at home. This is where having a good sound system adds a lot of stuff. It completely redefines the viewing experience. Entertainment cannot be just visuals only.
Sound adds the real depth, the feel, the essence, and without it, you are only receiving half the artistic intent of a scene.
To truly understand the value of what sound is all about, I want you to look beyond the basic acoustic limitations of modern televisions.

Today's displays are remarkably thin, which leaves absolutely no physical cabinet space for speaker drivers to move air. The result is a flat, lifeless acoustic signature. I have been testing a modular trio from Sony for quite some time, claiming to solve this problem.

This trio system consists of the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7 (Rs 99,990) handling the front and height channels, the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 (Rs 42,990) delivering the low-frequency rumble, and the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers (Rs 42,990) wrapping the room in immersive surround sound. Let me tell you all about my experience when I combined them to find out if this trio system is the best home theater setup that you can have.

The centerpiece of this entire system is the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7. Visually, it is a sleek, low-profile soundbar wrapped in an acoustic fabric that slips seamlessly under your television. But inside the chassis, it is an engineered powerhouse. The Bar 7 packs nine dedicated speaker units, including side-firing drivers and up-firing units designed to physically bounce height channels off your ceiling.

From an audiophile standpoint, what the Bar 7 does flawlessly is anchor the vocal clarity. Credit to its dedicated center channel processing, dialogues are crisp and well-separated from the chaotic background noise of an action sequence. It supports the heavy-hitting spatial formats like Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, and is even IMAX Enhanced.

However, if there is one caveat to the Bar 7 as a standalone unit, it is the lower frequency response. It delivers crystal-clear mids and highs, but because of its compact volume, it simply does not get low or loud enough on its own to provide a truly cinematic punch. I guess that's exactly why it requires the rest of the trio.

This is where the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 comes into play, and it completely transforms the acoustic signature of the system. A soundbar handles the intricate directional details, but a dedicated subwoofer is what gives the audio its physical weight and presence.
Armed with a 300W amplifier and a large 200mm driver unit, the Sub 8 handles the heavy lifting for the low-end frequencies. In the audio world, a good sub doesn't just make noise; it moves air.

You stop just hearing an explosion on screen and start actually feeling the shockwave reverberate through the floorboards. What impressed me the most is how well the crossover is managed. The Sub 8 delivers propulsive, controlled bass that grounds the action sequences without ever muddying the mid-range or overpowering the vocals coming from the Bar 7.

As pristine as the front stage and bass are, the system achieves true immersiveness when you add the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers. These two speakers add the 5.1 kind of depth that you absolutely need. When you install them and set them up behind the backside of where you sit, that placement makes things profoundly immersive.

It is here that Sony's 360 'Spatial Sound Mapping' goes into overdrive. The system does not just passively push sound to the back of the room; it mathematically generates multiple 'phantom speakers' in a dome around and above you.

When a helicopter flies past on the screen, you genuinely hear the rotors move seamlessly from the front Bar 7, across the ceiling, and fade into the Rear 8s behind you. All of a sudden, I started to feel as if I am genuinely watching a movie in a premium commercial theater. They elevate the soundstage from a flat, two-dimensional plane to a living, breathing environment.
This Sony trio is easily the easiest setup I have ever experienced. You simply place the units in their respective spots, plug them into a power outlet, and open the smartphone app.

The BRAVIA Connect app takes care of everything. There is no complicated calibration microphone to wave around the room. The system uses 'Sound Field Optimization', sending out a quick pulse of sound to digitally map your specific room's acoustic characteristics. Within seconds, it calibrates the sound field height and optimizes the spatial mapping for your exact seating position. And if you are an enthusiast who wants to tinker, the app allows for pro-level customizations, letting you adjust the sound field, voice modes, and individual rear speaker levels to perfectly match your preferences.

At times, if the content is not natively 5.1 or Dolby Atmos ready, the system can struggle slightly with the upmixing. When you are watching standard stereo broadcasts or compressed streaming video, the audio can become very heavy when the sound goes up. Because Sony's upmixing algorithm is aggressive in trying to utilize all the physical and phantom speakers, standard flat audio is pushed hard into the surround channels.

This can make the background score or ambient noise feel dense and overwhelming in the lower frequencies. Thankfully, it is quite normal when the vocals are active; dialogue never gets lost. But the balance you hear on a 4K Blu-ray can occasionally feel a bit artificially inflated on basic content.

If you are planning to invest in this setup, here is my practical take on getting the best out of it. First, running the Sound Field Optimization in the BRAVIA Connect app is non-negotiable; skipping it leaves the spatial audio flat, whereas running it properly maps the phantom speakers to your ceiling height and room dimensions.

Second, definitely make use of the app's 'Voice Mode' for poorly mixed movies where action effects tend to drown out dialogues, it isolates speech cleanly without distorting the rest of the mix. I think, buying the Bar 7 without the Sub 8 is an incomplete experience, so go for the trio to bring in a sense of authority that true home cinema demands.

For a few of you, I do not expect this trio to double as a dedicated audiophile Hi-Fi setup for stereo music streaming. And the reason is simple. In my opinion, this trio is tuned specifically for cinematic theatricality, where standard music tracks can occasionally feel a bit clinical or bass-heavy. If you're an enthusiast then do note that there are no manual multiband EQ controls (you rely on Sony's automated Sound Field profiles).

Then there is no alphanumeric LED display on the front grille, so you have to glance at the TV or phone app just to check volume levels and active codecs. Last but not least, there are occasional momentary audio dropouts over HDMI during dead-silent scenes where the bar momentarily sleeps and clips the very first syllable when audio resumes.

Despite that minor quirk with standard audio, Sony has proved their mettle in terms of what they have done with this ecosystem. The combination of the Bar 7, Sub 8, and Rear 8 delivers an expansive, surreal soundstage that redefines home entertainment. So yes, it is simply one of the best.
(Disclaimer: Himank Tripathi is an expert in the fields of consumer technology, lifestyle and automotive. Views shared are personal.)

content: Hubballi (Karnataka) [India], October 13 A day after Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar met Union Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister Pralhad Joshi in the national capital, security at the latter's residence in Hubballi district was tightened on Tuesday amid calls for a national highway blockade by the sugarcane farmers.

The farmers have intensified their demands while pressing for a hike in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for sugarcane. They have announced a road blockade on the National Highway. Farmers have also been demanding that their long-standing demands be implemented.
As this happened, a heavy police force was deployed, and barricades were erected on roads leading to the minister's residence.

The development comes amid an ongoing dispute over sugarcane pricing and alleged irregularities at sugar factories, with farmers raising concerns over weighing discrepancies, lower recorded harvest weights, alleged tampering with weighing machines and transportation-related fraud after harvesting.
Joshi met Karnataka CM Shivakumar at the former's residence in Delhi on Monday to discuss concerns raised by sugarcane farmers over pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season.
In a post on X, Joshi wrote, "Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who arrived at my residence in Delhi this evening, met me cordially.

"In this context, at meeting with sugarcane farmers, the major issues shared by the farmers were the govt advisory price for sugarcane, fraud and discrepancies in sugarcane weighing at sugar factories, factories showing lower harvest weights, tampering with weighing machines, and paying attention to transportation fraud after harvest. I informed the Chief Minister about these problems and requested resolution."

Meanwhile, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar wrote on X, "Met Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Joshi Pralhad, to discuss the concerns of Karnataka's sugarcane farmers regarding cane pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season."

"We discussed the need to ensure fair and remunerative prices for sugarcane growers and to address the concerns raised by our farmers. I urged the Union Government to consider Karnataka's views and safeguard the interests of sugarcane farmers."

Earlier on Monday, while speaking to Metrotimes, Shivakumar said, "I came here to discuss the sugarcane price issue. Farmers are demanding a higher price, but factories are unable to meet their demands due to heavy losses. This year, there has also been a severe drought. More than 200 farmers had come to meet me. I had also sent some of our ministers to discuss the issue."

"This matter needs to be discussed at the national level. It is not just Karnataka's problem. Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and every state where sugarcane is grown need to take a decision. There will be a process of consultation. We have said that we all need to work together to help everyone. The farmers should benefit, and the industries should also benefit. We will work on this issue," he added.

allArticles.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
allArticles.summary: Dubai [UAE], October 13 Indian skipper Shubman Gill achieved his record-extending fifth 'ICC Player of the Month' award for September 2026, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Tuesday
content: Dubai [UAE], October 13 Indian skipper Shubman Gill achieved his record-extending fifth 'ICC Player of the Month' award for September 2026, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Tuesday.
Gill, as per the ICC, won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza.
Gill scored 333 runs in India's first two ODIs against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets.
In the first ODI, in Thiruvananthapuram on 27 September, Gill made 110 off 108 balls as India chased down West Indies' 295/7. India reached the target of 296 in 41.4 overs.

Three days later in Guwahati, West Indies made 405/7, their first ODI total above 400. Gill, captaining India, responded with an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, including 26 fours and eight sixes, and India finished on 406/2 in 43.3 overs with 39 balls to spare. He reached his hundred in 62 balls, the fastest by an Indian captain in ODIs, and his double century in 117 balls, the fastest in ODI history.

It remains the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase. Gill and Rohit Sharma (101 off 75 balls) put on 255 for the opening wicket, India's highest partnership on home soil. The chase was the second-highest successful one in ODI history, behind only South Africa's 438/9 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.

"A very major incident occurred just a short while ago. As we have been saying repeatedly, the Punjab government is being run by a drug mafia. It seems that Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal, and Manish Sisodia are taking a lot of money from the drug mafia," Sirsa alleged.

"Just imagine, this kind of thing used to happen in America or Colombia, where those who spoke out against drugs were killed. Today, Punjab has become the same kind of state, where the police either torture people and put them in jail, or, as in today's incident, someone who was fighting against drugs was murdered. This shows the state of drug issues in Punjab," he added.

Sirsa's remarks come after Jhota, who was known for his activism against drugs in Mansa, was shot by a medical shop owner. He was taken to a hospital after sustaining bullet injuries and later succumbed to them.

The killing of Jhota has ignited a political firestorm with opposition leaders tearing into the Bhagwant Mann-led government alleging a failure of law and order and questioning the effectiveness of the state's campaign against drugs.

"The broad daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota a known and drug activist of Punjab only shows how powerful #DrugMafia is under the @AamAadmiParty govt! Politician-Police-Drug Mafia nexus rules the roost in Punjab," Khaira said in a post on X.
Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia alleged that Jhota was shot while recording drug dealers on camera.

allArticles.title: Review of  Sony BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7, Sub 8, Rear 8
allArticles.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
allArticles.summary: New Delhi [India], October 3 I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series a
content: New Delhi [India], October 3 I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series at home. This is where having a good sound system adds a lot of stuff. It completely redefines the viewing experience. Entertainment cannot be just visuals only.
Sound adds the real depth, the feel, the essence, and without it, you are only receiving half the artistic intent of a scene.
To truly understand the value of what sound is all about, I want you to look beyond the basic acoustic limitations of modern televisions.

Today's displays are remarkably thin, which leaves absolutely no physical cabinet space for speaker drivers to move air. The result is a flat, lifeless acoustic signature. I have been testing a modular trio from Sony for quite some time, claiming to solve this problem.

This trio system consists of the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7 (Rs 99,990) handling the front and height channels, the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 (Rs 42,990) delivering the low-frequency rumble, and the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers (Rs 42,990) wrapping the room in immersive surround sound. Let me tell you all about my experience when I combined them to find out if this trio system is the best home theater setup that you can have.

The centerpiece of this entire system is the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7. Visually, it is a sleek, low-profile soundbar wrapped in an acoustic fabric that slips seamlessly under your television. But inside the chassis, it is an engineered powerhouse. The Bar 7 packs nine dedicated speaker units, including side-firing drivers and up-firing units designed to physically bounce height channels off your ceiling.

From an audiophile standpoint, what the Bar 7 does flawlessly is anchor the vocal clarity. Credit to its dedicated center channel processing, dialogues are crisp and well-separated from the chaotic background noise of an action sequence. It supports the heavy-hitting spatial formats like Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, and is even IMAX Enhanced.

However, if there is one caveat to the Bar 7 as a standalone unit, it is the lower frequency response. It delivers crystal-clear mids and highs, but because of its compact volume, it simply does not get low or loud enough on its own to provide a truly cinematic punch. I guess that's exactly why it requires the rest of the trio.

This is where the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 comes into play, and it completely transforms the acoustic signature of the system. A soundbar handles the intricate directional details, but a dedicated subwoofer is what gives the audio its physical weight and presence.
Armed with a 300W amplifier and a large 200mm driver unit, the Sub 8 handles the heavy lifting for the low-end frequencies. In the audio world, a good sub doesn't just make noise; it moves air.

You stop just hearing an explosion on screen and start actually feeling the shockwave reverberate through the floorboards. What impressed me the most is how well the crossover is managed. The Sub 8 delivers propulsive, controlled bass that grounds the action sequences without ever muddying the mid-range or overpowering the vocals coming from the Bar 7.

As pristine as the front stage and bass are, the system achieves true immersiveness when you add the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers. These two speakers add the 5.1 kind of depth that you absolutely need. When you install them and set them up behind the backside of where you sit, that placement makes things profoundly immersive.

It is here that Sony's 360 'Spatial Sound Mapping' goes into overdrive. The system does not just passively push sound to the back of the room; it mathematically generates multiple 'phantom speakers' in a dome around and above you.

When a helicopter flies past on the screen, you genuinely hear the rotors move seamlessly from the front Bar 7, across the ceiling, and fade into the Rear 8s behind you. All of a sudden, I started to feel as if I am genuinely watching a movie in a premium commercial theater. They elevate the soundstage from a flat, two-dimensional plane to a living, breathing environment.
This Sony trio is easily the easiest setup I have ever experienced. You simply place the units in their respective spots, plug them into a power outlet, and open the smartphone app.

The BRAVIA Connect app takes care of everything. There is no complicated calibration microphone to wave around the room. The system uses 'Sound Field Optimization', sending out a quick pulse of sound to digitally map your specific room's acoustic characteristics. Within seconds, it calibrates the sound field height and optimizes the spatial mapping for your exact seating position. And if you are an enthusiast who wants to tinker, the app allows for pro-level customizations, letting you adjust the sound field, voice modes, and individual rear speaker levels to perfectly match your preferences.

At times, if the content is not natively 5.1 or Dolby Atmos ready, the system can struggle slightly with the upmixing. When you are watching standard stereo broadcasts or compressed streaming video, the audio can become very heavy when the sound goes up. Because Sony's upmixing algorithm is aggressive in trying to utilize all the physical and phantom speakers, standard flat audio is pushed hard into the surround channels.

This can make the background score or ambient noise feel dense and overwhelming in the lower frequencies. Thankfully, it is quite normal when the vocals are active; dialogue never gets lost. But the balance you hear on a 4K Blu-ray can occasionally feel a bit artificially inflated on basic content.

If you are planning to invest in this setup, here is my practical take on getting the best out of it. First, running the Sound Field Optimization in the BRAVIA Connect app is non-negotiable; skipping it leaves the spatial audio flat, whereas running it properly maps the phantom speakers to your ceiling height and room dimensions.

Second, definitely make use of the app's 'Voice Mode' for poorly mixed movies where action effects tend to drown out dialogues, it isolates speech cleanly without distorting the rest of the mix. I think, buying the Bar 7 without the Sub 8 is an incomplete experience, so go for the trio to bring in a sense of authority that true home cinema demands.

For a few of you, I do not expect this trio to double as a dedicated audiophile Hi-Fi setup for stereo music streaming. And the reason is simple. In my opinion, this trio is tuned specifically for cinematic theatricality, where standard music tracks can occasionally feel a bit clinical or bass-heavy. If you're an enthusiast then do note that there are no manual multiband EQ controls (you rely on Sony's automated Sound Field profiles).

Then there is no alphanumeric LED display on the front grille, so you have to glance at the TV or phone app just to check volume levels and active codecs. Last but not least, there are occasional momentary audio dropouts over HDMI during dead-silent scenes where the bar momentarily sleeps and clips the very first syllable when audio resumes.

Despite that minor quirk with standard audio, Sony has proved their mettle in terms of what they have done with this ecosystem. The combination of the Bar 7, Sub 8, and Rear 8 delivers an expansive, surreal soundstage that redefines home entertainment. So yes, it is simply one of the best.
(Disclaimer: Himank Tripathi is an expert in the fields of consumer technology, lifestyle and automotive. Views shared are personal.)

allArticles.summary: New Delhi [India], October 13: Bisleri International, India's leading packaged drinking water brand, collaborated with the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026 as its Official Hydration Partner. Held at Dr A
content: New Delhi [India], October 13: Bisleri International, India's leading packaged drinking water brand, collaborated with the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026 as its Official Hydration Partner. Held at Dr Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, the festival brought together over 1,000 school students, and educators, climate experts, artists and innovators under the theme 'AI & Climate: Reimagining the Future Together.' The festival forms part of the Purple Umbrella Foundation's wider mission to empower one million young climate champions. Bisleri's flagship Bottles for Change initiative played a central role in sensitising young participants on responsible plastic waste management, recycling and circularity.

As part of the collaboration, Bisleri created a dedicated 'Greener Promise' experience designed to help students see plastic waste as a resource that can be recovered, recycled and reimagined. At the centre of the experience was Wings of Change, an art installation created from 2,000 used PET bottles, using creative expression to bring the idea of circularity to life. The company also showcased its Benches of Dreams, made from recycled plastic, offering participants a tangible example of how discarded material can return to everyday use in a new form.

Speaking about the association, Dr Angelo George, CEO, Bisleri International, said, "It is vital to engage young people in conversations about environmental responsibility and inspire them to turn awareness into action. The Purple Umbrella Festival offers students an opportunity to learn, exchange ideas and make more sustainable choices in their everyday lives. Through Bottles for Change, we continue to build awareness of responsible plastic waste management and recycling, encouraging everyone to play their part in creating a cleaner, greener planet."

Aligned with the Purple Umbrella Foundation's larger mission of empowering one million young climate champions, the festival encouraged young people to explore climate change as creators, problem-solvers and emerging climate champions. Theatre, film, technology, innovation and dialogue were central to these interactions. The programme featured Theatre for Climate, short films and documentaries, student innovations, climate talks, a Climate, Health & Mental Wellbeing Conclave, and the Climate & Heritage Quiz.

Neeraj Kumar, Founder, Purple Umbrella Foundation, said, "The Purple Umbrella Festival is designed to encourage young people to think creatively about climate challenges and the role they can play in addressing them. Bisleri's participation adds an important dimension to the festival by helping students understand the importance of responsible plastic waste management and recycling through hands-on experiences."

Bisleri's participation at the festival reinforced its commitment to advancing responsible plastic waste management and environmental awareness among young people. Through Bottles for Change, the company continues to promote recycling and circularity while encouraging more responsible waste-management choices at the individual and community level.

breakingNews.title: Security tightens outside Union Minister Pralhad Joshi's Hubballi residence as sugarcane farmers intensify protest
breakingNews.author: Metrotimes News Bureau
breakingNews.summary: Hubballi (Karnataka) [India], October 13 A day after Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar met Union Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister Pralhad Joshi in the national capital, sec
content: Hubballi (Karnataka) [India], October 13 A day after Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar met Union Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister Pralhad Joshi in the national capital, security at the latter's residence in Hubballi district was tightened on Tuesday amid calls for a national highway blockade by the sugarcane farmers.

The farmers have intensified their demands while pressing for a hike in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for sugarcane. They have announced a road blockade on the National Highway. Farmers have also been demanding that their long-standing demands be implemented.
As this happened, a heavy police force was deployed, and barricades were erected on roads leading to the minister's residence.

The development comes amid an ongoing dispute over sugarcane pricing and alleged irregularities at sugar factories, with farmers raising concerns over weighing discrepancies, lower recorded harvest weights, alleged tampering with weighing machines and transportation-related fraud after harvesting.
Joshi met Karnataka CM Shivakumar at the former's residence in Delhi on Monday to discuss concerns raised by sugarcane farmers over pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season.
In a post on X, Joshi wrote, "Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who arrived at my residence in Delhi this evening, met me cordially.

"In this context, at meeting with sugarcane farmers, the major issues shared by the farmers were the govt advisory price for sugarcane, fraud and discrepancies in sugarcane weighing at sugar factories, factories showing lower harvest weights, tampering with weighing machines, and paying attention to transportation fraud after harvest. I informed the Chief Minister about these problems and requested resolution."

Meanwhile, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar wrote on X, "Met Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Joshi Pralhad, to discuss the concerns of Karnataka's sugarcane farmers regarding cane pricing for the 2026–27 sugar season."

"We discussed the need to ensure fair and remunerative prices for sugarcane growers and to address the concerns raised by our farmers. I urged the Union Government to consider Karnataka's views and safeguard the interests of sugarcane farmers."

Earlier on Monday, while speaking to Metrotimes, Shivakumar said, "I came here to discuss the sugarcane price issue. Farmers are demanding a higher price, but factories are unable to meet their demands due to heavy losses. This year, there has also been a severe drought. More than 200 farmers had come to meet me. I had also sent some of our ministers to discuss the issue."

"This matter needs to be discussed at the national level. It is not just Karnataka's problem. Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and every state where sugarcane is grown need to take a decision. There will be a process of consultation. We have said that we all need to work together to help everyone. The farmers should benefit, and the industries should also benefit. We will work on this issue," he added.
